---- MODULE W4Od10m4p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxEpoch, QueueCap

VARIABLES queue, currentEpoch, authController, authHistory, lastActor, lastEpoch

vars == <<queue, currentEpoch, authController, authHistory, lastActor, lastEpoch>>

\* The bounded queue models a signalling block's inbox of control messages.
\* Backpressure blocks new sends once QueueCap messages are pending.
\* Messages may be picked from the queue in any order (reordering), and a
\* message is applied only if it matches the currently authorized
\* controller and epoch; otherwise it is dropped as unauthorized/stale.

Msgs == [ctrl : Controllers, epoch : 1..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \subseteq Msgs
  /\ currentEpoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
  /\ authController \in Controllers
  /\ authHistory \subseteq Msgs
  /\ lastActor \in Controllers \cup {"None"}
  /\ lastEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch

Init ==
  \E a \in Controllers :
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ currentEpoch = 1
    /\ authController = a
    /\ authHistory = {[ctrl |-> a, epoch |-> 1]}
    /\ lastActor = "None"
    /\ lastEpoch = 0

Enqueue(c, e) ==
  /\ Cardinality(queue) < QueueCap
  /\ e <= currentEpoch
  /\ queue' = queue \cup {[ctrl |-> c, epoch |-> e]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<currentEpoch, authController, authHistory, lastActor, lastEpoch>>

\* Authority handover: the interlocking rotates control of the block to a
\* new controller and bumps the epoch, recording the grant in authHistory.
Rotate ==
  /\ currentEpoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \E newC \in Controllers \ {authController} :
       /\ currentEpoch' = currentEpoch + 1
       /\ authController' = newC
       /\ authHistory' = authHistory \cup {[ctrl |-> newC, epoch |-> currentEpoch + 1]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, lastActor, lastEpoch>>

\* A pending message is applied only when it is from the currently
\* authorized controller and stamped with the current epoch.
ApplyValid(m) ==
  /\ m \in queue
  /\ m.ctrl = authController
  /\ m.epoch = currentEpoch
  /\ queue' = queue \ {m}
  /\ lastActor' = m.ctrl
  /\ lastEpoch' = m.epoch
  /\ UNCHANGED <<currentEpoch, authController, authHistory>>

\* An unauthorized or stale message is discarded without effect.
DropStale(m) ==
  /\ m \in queue
  /\ ~(m.ctrl = authController /\ m.epoch = currentEpoch)
  /\ queue' = queue \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<currentEpoch, authController, authHistory, lastActor, lastEpoch>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, e \in 1..MaxEpoch : Enqueue(c, e)
  \/ Rotate
  \/ \E m \in queue : ApplyValid(m)
  \/ \E m \in queue : DropStale(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: any control action that actually took effect must correspond to
\* a genuine authorization grant on record -- this rules out an
\* unauthorized controller or a stale (superseded-epoch) message ever
\* having taken effect on the block.
NoStaleControl ==
  (lastActor # "None") => ([ctrl |-> lastActor, epoch |-> lastEpoch] \in authHistory)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Controllers = {c1, c2}
  MaxEpoch = 2
  QueueCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleControl

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway signalling block maintains a bounded inbox of control messages sent
by trackside controllers requesting to hold or release the block. The inbox
applies backpressure: a controller cannot enqueue a new message once the
inbox already holds QueueCap pending messages. Because messages can be
reordered in transit, the block does not process its inbox in send order;
instead it may pick any pending message to consider next. Control of the
block is periodically handed over from one controller to the next, which
advances an epoch counter and records the new grant of authority. A pending
message only takes effect on the block if it comes from the controller
currently holding authority and carries the current epoch number; any
message from a controller that is no longer authorized, or that carries an
epoch from before the last handover, is recognized as unauthorized or stale
and is discarded without effect.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No control action ever takes effect on the block unless it
was issued by the controller and epoch actually authorized at that time,
i.e. no unauthorized or stale participant can affect the block state.

---- MODULE W4Od9m5p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS SLOTS, NoSlot, Quorum

ASSUME NoSlot \notin SLOTS
ASSUME Quorum \in Nat

VARIABLES pool, alloc, req, votes

vars == <<pool, alloc, req, votes>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ pool \subseteq SLOTS
  /\ alloc \in [{1,2} -> SLOTS \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ req \in [{1,2} -> SLOTS \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ votes \in [{1,2} -> 0..Quorum]

Init ==
  /\ pool = SLOTS
  /\ alloc = [i \in {1,2} |-> NoSlot]
  /\ req = [i \in {1,2} |-> NoSlot]
  /\ votes = [i \in {1,2} |-> 0]

\* An instance proposes to claim a free slot from the shared pool and resets its quorum vote tally.
Propose(i) ==
  /\ req[i] = NoSlot
  /\ alloc[i] = NoSlot
  /\ \E s \in pool :
       req' = [req EXCEPT ![i] = s]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, alloc>>

Vote(i) ==
  /\ req[i] # NoSlot
  /\ votes[i] < Quorum
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, alloc, req>>

\* Commit allocates only if quorum was reached AND the slot is still actually free in the shared pool; this recheck is what stops both instances from taking the same slot.
Commit(i) ==
  /\ req[i] # NoSlot
  /\ votes[i] >= Quorum
  /\ req[i] \in pool
  /\ pool' = pool \ {req[i]}
  /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![i] = req[i]]
  /\ req' = [req EXCEPT ![i] = NoSlot]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = 0]

\* If the requested slot was claimed by the other instance while quorum was forming, the stale request is rejected rather than committed.
Reject(i) ==
  /\ req[i] # NoSlot
  /\ req[i] \notin pool
  /\ req' = [req EXCEPT ![i] = NoSlot]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, alloc>>

Release(i) ==
  /\ alloc[i] # NoSlot
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {alloc[i]}
  /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![i] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<req, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ Propose(1) \/ Propose(2)
  \/ Vote(1) \/ Vote(2)
  \/ Commit(1) \/ Commit(2)
  \/ Reject(1) \/ Reject(2)
  \/ Release(1) \/ Release(2)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Propose(1))
  /\ WF_vars(Propose(2))
  /\ WF_vars(Vote(1))
  /\ WF_vars(Vote(2))
  /\ SF_vars(Commit(1))
  /\ SF_vars(Commit(2))
  /\ SF_vars(Reject(1))
  /\ SF_vars(Reject(2))

\* SAFETY: no double allocation -- the two instances never end up holding the same slot, and any slot marked allocated is not simultaneously shown free in the shared pool.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  /\ (alloc[1] # NoSlot /\ alloc[2] # NoSlot) => alloc[1] # alloc[2]
  /\ alloc[1] # NoSlot => alloc[1] \notin pool
  /\ alloc[2] # NoSlot => alloc[2] \notin pool

\* LIVENESS: every pending request is eventually resolved, either granted (committed into an allocation) or rejected (because the slot went to the other instance).
EventualResolution ==
  /\ (req[1] # NoSlot ~> req[1] = NoSlot)
  /\ (req[2] # NoSlot ~> req[2] = NoSlot)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  SLOTS = {s1, s2}
  NoSlot = NoSlot
  Quorum = 2

INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
PROPERTY EventualResolution

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In a power-grid load shedder, two independent shedding instances (control agents for two separate feeder zones) draw allocation slots from a single shared pool of shedding slots. Neither instance owns any slot outright: whenever an instance needs to shed load through a slot, it proposes taking one from the shared pool and gathers votes from a quorum of monitoring nodes before the allocation is committed. Because both instances draw from the very same pool, a slot that looked available when a proposal was raised can be claimed by the other instance first; the mechanism therefore rechecks pool membership at commit time, granting the slot only if it is still free and otherwise rejecting the stale request so the instance can retry. Allocated slots are eventually released back to the shared pool once no longer needed, making them available again.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no shedding slot is ever held as an active allocation by both instances at the same time, and no slot marked as allocated is ever simultaneously left shown as free in the shared pool.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every allocation request an instance raises against the shared pool is eventually resolved, either granted into a committed allocation or rejected because the slot went to the other instance.

---- MODULE W4Od8m6p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Models a course-registration seat guarded by a lease with an expiry clock.
\* Grant/Renew bump an epoch counter; network messages (msgs) carry the
\* epoch they were issued under and can be delivered in any order (reordering).
\* Safety intent: a participant may only act as the registrant if it is the
\* current owner, its message is not stale (epoch matches), and the lease
\* has not expired -- no unauthorized or stale participant can act.

CONSTANTS Students, NoOne, MaxTime, LeaseLen, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES owner, epoch, expiry, clock, active, msgs

TypeOK ==
  /\ owner \in Students \cup {NoOne}
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ expiry \in 0..(MaxTime + LeaseLen)
  /\ clock \in 0..MaxTime
  /\ active \in Students \cup {NoOne}
  /\ msgs \subseteq [type : {"grant"}, student : Students, epoch : 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
  /\ owner = NoOne
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ expiry = 0
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ active = NoOne
  /\ msgs = {}

\* Advancing the clock past a lease's expiry atomically revokes both the
\* ownership and any active status riding on it, closing the staleness
\* window at the instant expiry actually occurs.
Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxTime
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ IF owner # NoOne /\ clock + 1 >= expiry
       THEN /\ owner' = NoOne
            /\ active' = NoOne
       ELSE /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, active>>
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, expiry, msgs>>

Grant(s) ==
  /\ owner = NoOne
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ owner' = s
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ expiry' = clock + LeaseLen
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[type |-> "grant", student |-> s, epoch |-> epoch + 1]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, active>>

\* Renewing an existing lease bumps the epoch, which silently invalidates
\* any older in-flight grant messages still sitting in msgs.
Renew(s) ==
  /\ owner = s
  /\ clock < expiry
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ expiry' = clock + LeaseLen
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[type |-> "grant", student |-> s, epoch |-> epoch + 1]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, clock, active>>

\* A student can only start acting as the registrant if the message it
\* holds names the current epoch and the lease has not expired: a
\* reordered, stale message (an old epoch) is rejected here.
Deliver(s) ==
  /\ \E m \in msgs :
       /\ m.student = s
       /\ m.epoch = epoch
       /\ clock < expiry
       /\ active' = s
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, epoch, expiry, clock, msgs>>

Next ==
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E s \in Students : Grant(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Renew(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Deliver(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<owner, epoch, expiry, clock, active, msgs>>

\* Safety: whenever some student is acting as the active registrant, it
\* must be the true current lease owner and the lease must not be expired.
NoStaleActive == active # NoOne => (active = owner /\ clock < expiry)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  s1 = s1
  s2 = s2
  Students = {s1, s2}
  NoOne = NoOne
  MaxTime = 2
  LeaseLen = 2
  MaxEpoch = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleActive
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A university course-registration system grants exclusive registration rights to a course seat using a lease with an explicit expiry. A registrar service can grant the lease to a student when the seat is free, and the current lease holder may renew it before it expires. Each grant or renewal is tagged with a monotonically increasing epoch number and produces a network notification message announcing the new epoch; because the network can reorder messages, older notifications from a previous epoch may still be in flight and could be delivered after a newer grant or renewal has already superseded them. A student becomes the "active" registrant for the seat only by consuming one of these notifications, and must check that its epoch matches the seat's current epoch and that the lease has not yet expired before treating the notification as valid; when a lease expires outright, both the ownership and any active status tied to it are revoked. The twist is that stale, reordered notifications from an earlier epoch are always present as candidates for delivery, so the mechanism's correctness hinges on epoch-and-freshness checking rather than message ordering.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever some student is acting as the active registrant of the seat, that student must be the seat's true current lease owner and the lease must not yet have expired.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS T1, T2, NoOwner

Trains == {T1, T2}

VARIABLES ver, owner, snapshot, mode, applied

vars == <<ver, owner, snapshot, mode, applied>>

\* The shared record is the pair (owner, ver); trains update it only via a
\* compare-and-swap against a version they previously read (snapshot).
\* "slow" is a lifecycle state that delays a train's CAS attempt but never
\* removes it from progress -- fairness still forces it to act eventually.

TypeOK ==
  /\ ver \in 0..6
  /\ owner \in Trains \cup {NoOwner}
  /\ snapshot \in [Trains -> 0..6]
  /\ mode \in [Trains -> {"idle", "pending", "slow", "done"}]
  /\ applied \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]

StateConstraint == ver <= 4

Init ==
  /\ ver = 0
  /\ owner = NoOwner
  /\ snapshot = [t \in Trains |-> 0]
  /\ mode = [t \in Trains |-> "idle"]
  /\ applied = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]

StartUpdate(t) ==
  /\ mode[t] = "idle"
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![t] = ver]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![t] = "pending"]
  /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner>>

GoSlow(t) ==
  /\ mode[t] = "pending"
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![t] = "slow"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner, snapshot, applied>>

\* The CAS itself: it succeeds only if the register's version still matches
\* what the train read; otherwise the update is superseded, never lost.
AttemptCAS(t) ==
  /\ mode[t] \in {"pending", "slow"}
  /\ IF snapshot[t] = ver
     THEN /\ ver' = ver + 1
          /\ owner' = t
          /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
     ELSE /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner>>
          /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![t] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED snapshot

Reset(t) ==
  /\ mode[t] = "done"
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner, snapshot, applied>>

StartT1 == StartUpdate(T1)
StartT2 == StartUpdate(T2)
CasT1 == AttemptCAS(T1)
CasT2 == AttemptCAS(T2)
SlowT1 == GoSlow(T1)
SlowT2 == GoSlow(T2)
ResetT1 == Reset(T1)
ResetT2 == Reset(T2)

Next ==
  \/ StartT1 \/ StartT2
  \/ SlowT1 \/ SlowT2
  \/ CasT1 \/ CasT2
  \/ ResetT1 \/ ResetT2

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(StartT1) /\ WF_vars(StartT2)
        /\ WF_vars(CasT1) /\ WF_vars(CasT2)
        /\ WF_vars(ResetT1) /\ WF_vars(ResetT2)

\* No lost updates: a train's belief that its CAS succeeded stays coherent
\* with the shared record -- it truly is the owner of the current version
\* exactly when no one else has advanced the register since.
NoLostUpdate ==
  \A t \in Trains:
    (mode[t] = "done" /\ applied[t]) => (owner = t <=> ver = snapshot[t] + 1)

\* Liveness: the slow train's pending update is never stuck forever -- it
\* is eventually applied (its CAS wins) or superseded (its CAS loses).
SlowUpdateResolves == (mode[T2] \in {"pending", "slow"}) ~> (mode[T2] = "done")

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  T1 = t1
  T2 = t2
  NoOwner = NoOwner

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoLostUpdate

PROPERTY SlowUpdateResolves

CONSTRAINT StateConstraint

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In a subway signalling block system, two trains (T1 and T2) approaching the
same block share a single record that names the block's current owner and a
version counter. A train wants to claim or update the block by reading the
record's version, computing its intended change, and then issuing a
compare-and-swap: the write is installed only if the version is still what
the train read; otherwise the write is rejected because someone else has
already moved the record forward. A train may become slow -- it can dawdle
for an arbitrary number of steps between reading the version and attempting
its compare-and-swap -- but it never fails outright, so it always eventually
attempts the swap. Because the swap is guarded by the version check, a slow
train's stale attempt is cleanly rejected instead of silently clobbering a
newer update, so no accepted update is ever lost even though the record has
no locks, only the compare-and-swap register.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a train believes its compare-and-swap succeeded, the shared record's recorded owner and version agree with that belief exactly when nobody has advanced the record since, so no train's applied update is ever silently overwritten or misattributed.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The slow train's pending update is eventually either applied (its compare-and-swap wins) or superseded (its compare-and-swap loses to a newer version), never stuck forever.

---- MODULE W4Od7m7p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, MinCap, MaxCap

VARIABLES cas, claimant, capacity, load, claimLoad, claimCap

\* cas is the compare-and-swap register guarding the one-shot release:
\* FREE -> CLAIMED -> DONE, and DONE is absorbing (never swaps back).
CapRange == MinCap .. MaxCap

vars == <<cas, claimant, capacity, load, claimLoad, claimCap>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ cas \in {"FREE", "CLAIMED", "DONE"}
  /\ claimant \in Cranes \cup {"none"}
  /\ capacity \in CapRange
  /\ load \in 0..(MaxCap + 1)
  /\ claimLoad \in 0..(MaxCap + 1)
  /\ claimCap \in CapRange

Init ==
  /\ cas = "FREE"
  /\ claimant = "none"
  /\ capacity \in CapRange
  /\ load = 0
  /\ claimLoad = 0
  /\ claimCap = MinCap

\* A crane may swap FREE -> CLAIMED only while there is real headroom, and it
\* snapshots the load/capacity it observed as the record of that permission.
Claim(c) ==
  /\ cas = "FREE"
  /\ load < capacity
  /\ cas' = "CLAIMED"
  /\ claimant' = c
  /\ claimLoad' = load
  /\ claimCap' = capacity
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, load>>

\* The claiming crane may back off without committing (e.g. capacity later
\* dropped and the claim went stale).
AbortClaim ==
  /\ cas = "CLAIMED"
  /\ cas' = "FREE"
  /\ claimant' = "none"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, load, claimLoad, claimCap>>

\* The irreversible release: CLAIMED -> DONE, forever after. This can only
\* ever fire once total per run, since Claim can never re-enter DONE.
CommitMove ==
  /\ cas = "CLAIMED"
  /\ load < capacity
  /\ cas' = "DONE"
  /\ load' = load + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<claimant, capacity, claimLoad, claimCap>>

\* Runtime twist: yard capacity can be raised or lowered independently of any
\* outstanding claim, possibly invalidating it before it commits.
AdjustCapacity ==
  \E nc \in CapRange :
    /\ nc # capacity
    /\ capacity' = nc
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cas, claimant, load, claimLoad, claimCap>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : Claim(c)
  \/ AbortClaim
  \/ CommitMove
  \/ AdjustCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: whenever the register shows the release completed, it completed
\* for a genuine crane whose claim really did have headroom when taken, and
\* load reflects exactly that one completed release -- i.e. the one-shot
\* action, if done at all, was done at most once and legitimately so.
OnceOnly ==
  cas = "DONE" =>
    /\ claimant \in Cranes
    /\ claimLoad < claimCap
    /\ load = claimLoad + 1

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cranes = {c1, c2}
  MinCap = 1
  MaxCap = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnceOnly
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In a container-ship crane yard, cranes compete to perform a single irreversible
action: physically releasing a container onto the yard stack (a move that,
once done, cannot be undone or repeated for that slot). A compare-and-swap
style register (cas) coordinates this: a crane must first swap the register
from FREE to CLAIMED to earn the exclusive right to commit the release; only
the crane holding the CLAIMED state may swap it onward to DONE, and once DONE
the register can never return to FREE or CLAIMED, so the release can happen at
most once. The yard's capacity (how many containers it can still accept) is
not fixed -- yard operators may raise or lower it at runtime (e.g. reclaiming
space, blocking off flooded sections), independently of any outstanding claim.
A crane may only claim the register when there is headroom (load < capacity),
and it snapshots that claim's load/capacity at claim time as its authorization
record; it may also abort a stale claim without committing. This models
whether the one-shot commit, whenever it has occurred, really was backed by a
legitimate, headroom-respecting claim, even though capacity itself may have
drifted since.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the crane's release action has completed (cas = DONE), it completed at most once, for a real crane, whose originating claim genuinely had load below capacity at the moment it was taken.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m5p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Proposals, Quorum, MaxRound

VARIABLES schedule, round, curProposal, msgs, acked, committed

vars == <<schedule, round, curProposal, msgs, acked, committed>>

\* A vote message records only the round it belongs to and the voting node;
\* the proposal value for that round is implicit, so a delayed (reordered)
\* vote from a round that has since moved on is identifiable by round alone.
Message == [rnd: 0..MaxRound, vt: Nodes]

Init ==
  /\ schedule = "None"
  /\ round = 0
  /\ curProposal \in Proposals
  /\ msgs = {}
  /\ acked = {}
  /\ committed = FALSE

\* Node n casts a vote (ack) for the schedule change proposed this round,
\* at most once per round so its vote is guaranteed to eventually drain.
Vote(n) ==
  /\ n \notin acked
  /\ ~ \E m \in msgs : m.rnd = round /\ m.vt = n
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[rnd |-> round, vt |-> n]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<schedule, round, curProposal, acked, committed>>

AnyVote == \E n \in Nodes : Vote(n)

\* Deliver one message chosen from the whole in-flight set, in any order,
\* modeling reordering. A vote whose round no longer matches the current
\* round is stale and is discarded instead of being counted toward quorum.
Deliver ==
  \E m \in msgs :
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
    /\ IF m.rnd = round
       THEN acked' = acked \cup {m.vt}
       ELSE acked' = acked
    /\ UNCHANGED <<schedule, round, curProposal, committed>>

\* Commit the proposal to the shared OR-schedule record once a genuine
\* quorum of round-consistent acks has accumulated; this is the only
\* action that ever writes the shared record.
Commit ==
  /\ ~committed
  /\ Cardinality(acked) >= Quorum
  /\ schedule' = curProposal
  /\ committed' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, curProposal, msgs, acked>>

\* Open the next scheduling round once the previous one has committed.
NextRound ==
  /\ committed
  /\ round < MaxRound
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ curProposal' \in Proposals
  /\ acked' = {}
  /\ committed' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<schedule, msgs>>

Next == AnyVote \/ Deliver \/ Commit \/ NextRound

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(AnyVote)
  /\ WF_vars(Deliver)
  /\ WF_vars(Commit)
  /\ WF_vars(NextRound)

\* SAFETY / no lost updates: whenever a round is marked committed, the
\* shared schedule record actually equals that round's decided proposal
\* and is backed by a real quorum of round-consistent acks -- a stale or
\* reordered vote can never substitute for a genuine quorum, so the
\* record can never appear committed to a value nobody actually decided.
ScheduleQuorumCoherence ==
  committed => (schedule = curProposal /\ Cardinality(acked) >= Quorum)

\* LIVENESS: despite arbitrary reordering of vote messages, the quorum
\* mechanism keeps making progress -- the schedule reaches a genuine
\* quorum-backed commit again and again, not just once by luck.
EventualCommit == []<>committed

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
  Proposals = {a, b}
  Quorum = 2
  MaxRound = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ScheduleQuorumCoherence

PROPERTY EventualCommit

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler keeps a single shared record describing
which procedure is booked into an OR slot. Any update to that record must be
ratified by quorum voting: a proposed change to the schedule only takes
effect once a quorum of the coordinating nodes (charge-nurse stations) have
acknowledged it for the current scheduling round. Acknowledgement messages
travel over a network where they can be reordered or delayed, so a vote cast
for an earlier round can arrive after a new round has already begun; the
mechanism must recognize such a vote as stale and discard it rather than let
it be miscounted toward the current round's quorum, which is what would
otherwise cause a lost or corrupted update to the shared record. Once a
round's proposal is genuinely quorum-acknowledged, the schedule is updated
and the next scheduling round opens.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a round is marked committed, the shared OR-schedule
record equals that round's decided proposal and is backed by an actual
quorum of round-consistent acknowledgements, so no reordered/stale vote can
ever masquerade as, or corrupt, a real quorum-committed update.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Despite arbitrary reordering of acknowledgement messages,

\* A library's book-reservation branches sit on a token ring: only the branch
\* holding the token may edit the shared reservation record for a book.
\* The network can reorder token-grant messages, so each grant carries a
\* generation number; a receiver only accepts a message whose generation
\* matches the current one, and stale reordered messages are simply dropped.

CONSTANTS N, MaxGen

Nodes == 1..N
RingNext(n) == IF n = N THEN 1 ELSE n + 1

VARIABLES tokenHolders, inCriticalSection, tokenGen, inTransit, lastCommitted

Init ==
  /\ tokenHolders = {1}
  /\ inCriticalSection = {}
  /\ tokenGen = 0
  /\ inTransit = {}
  /\ lastCommitted = 0

Send(n) ==
  /\ n \in tokenHolders
  /\ n \notin inCriticalSection
  /\ tokenGen < MaxGen
  /\ inTransit' = inTransit \cup {[dest |-> RingNext(n), gen |-> tokenGen + 1]}
  /\ tokenGen' = tokenGen + 1
  /\ tokenHolders' = tokenHolders \ {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inCriticalSection, lastCommitted>>

\* Only a message whose generation matches the live one may be delivered;
\* reordered messages from older generations cannot be mistaken for it.
Receive ==
  /\ \E m \in inTransit:
       /\ m.gen = tokenGen
       /\ tokenHolders' = tokenHolders \cup {m.dest}
       /\ inTransit' = inTransit \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenGen, inCriticalSection, lastCommitted>>

\* Explicitly garbage-collect stale, reordered messages from the network.
DropStale ==
  /\ \E m \in inTransit:
       /\ m.gen < tokenGen
       /\ inTransit' = inTransit \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolders, tokenGen, inCriticalSection, lastCommitted>>

Enter(n) ==
  /\ n \in tokenHolders
  /\ inCriticalSection = {}
  /\ inCriticalSection' = {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolders, tokenGen, inTransit, lastCommitted>>

ExitCS(n) ==
  /\ n \in inCriticalSection
  /\ inCriticalSection' = {}
  /\ lastCommitted' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolders, tokenGen, inTransit>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes: Send(n) \/ Enter(n) \/ ExitCS(n)
  \/ Receive
  \/ DropStale

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* branch may be editing the book record, and whoever is editing must
\* actually be the current token holder (not a stale/duplicate grantee).
MutualExclusion ==
  /\ Cardinality(inCriticalSection) <= 1
  /\ Cardinality(tokenHolders) <= 1
  /\ (inCriticalSection # {} => inCriticalSection \subseteq tokenHolders)

---- MODULE W4Od0m0p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, CrashProne, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, owner, localEpoch, crashed, pending

vars == <<epoch, owner, localEpoch, crashed, pending>>

\* The OR schedule is versioned by `epoch`. A writer may only commit if its
\* cached epoch still matches the current one (optimistic locking). A stale
\* writer must retry: re-read the epoch, then attempt the commit again.

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..(MaxEpoch-1)
  /\ owner \in Participants \cup {"none"}
  /\ localEpoch \in [Participants -> 0..(MaxEpoch-1)]
  /\ crashed \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ pending \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ owner = "none"
  /\ localEpoch = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
  /\ crashed = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]
  /\ pending = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]

\* A non-crashed, idle participant submits a scheduling request, stamping it
\* with the epoch it currently observes.
Request(p) ==
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ ~pending[p]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ localEpoch' = [localEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, crashed>>

\* Commit only succeeds if the writer's stamp still matches: this is the
\* optimistic-locking check that rejects stale or unauthorized writers.
Commit(p) ==
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ pending[p]
  /\ localEpoch[p] = epoch
  /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % MaxEpoch
  /\ owner' = p
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ localEpoch' = [localEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = (epoch + 1) % MaxEpoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* A stale writer (its stamp lost the race) discovers the mismatch and
\* refreshes its view of the epoch before it may retry the commit.
RetryStale(p) ==
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ pending[p]
  /\ localEpoch[p] # epoch
  /\ localEpoch' = [localEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, pending, crashed>>

\* The twist: the crash-prone participant may go silent at any time,
\* permanently, without ever releasing or completing its pending request.
CrashSilently ==
  /\ ~crashed[CrashProne]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![CrashProne] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, localEpoch, pending>>

Next ==
  \/ (\E p \in Participants: Request(p) \/ Commit(p) \/ RetryStale(p))
  \/ CrashSilently

\* SAFETY: the participant recorded as owning the current epoch must never
\* be a stale writer: its cached stamp must always match the live epoch
\* (a crashed writer can never reach this state at all, since Commit's
\* guard already excludes crashed participants from acting).
OwnerNotStale ==
  owner # "none" => localEpoch[owner] = epoch

Reliable == CHOOSE p \in Participants : p # CrashProne

\* LIVENESS: a non-crash-prone participant's pending request is always
\* eventually committed, despite races with a stale/crashing peer.
EventualCommit == pending[Reliable] ~> ~pending[Reliable]

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Request(Reliable))
  /\ WF_vars(RetryStale(Reliable))
  /\ SF_vars(Commit(Reliable))

\* Two independent leader-election instances each track their own epoch/generation
\* but contend for one shared physical lock pool via a single fencing token.

        /\ grantEpoch = 0
        /\ fired = FALSE
        /\ firedToken = 0

\* Failover: instance i's controller is re-elected into a strictly newer generation.
Reelect(i) == /\ ~fired
              /\ epoch[i] < MaxEpoch
              /\ epoch' = [epoch EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<grantee, grantEpoch, fired, firedToken>>

\* Instance i claims the shared pool grant, but only with a strictly fresher epoch
\* than the fencing token on file -- this is what stops a stale leader from either
\* instance displacing a newer one on the shared pool.

            /\ grantee' = i
            /\ grantEpoch' = epoch[i]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, fired, firedToken>>

\* taken by the current grantee, and only while its own epoch still matches the
\* fencing token it was granted under -- i.e. it has not since been superseded.

        /\ grantee # NoInst
        /\ epoch[grantee] = grantEpoch
        /\ fired' = TRUE
        /\ firedToken' = grantEpoch
        /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantee, grantEpoch>>

        \/ \E i \in Instances : Grant(i)
        \/ Revoke

\* matches both the shared fencing counter and the firer's own live epoch -- i.e.
\* the irreversible action was never taken under a stale or superseded generation.

                             /\ grantEpoch = firedToken)

  /\ lobbyEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch

  /\ capacity \in Capacities
  /\ queue = {}
  /\ lobby = {}
  /\ lobbyEpoch = 0

  /\ queue # {}
  /\ commitCount[epoch] = 0

  /\ queue' = queue \cup lobby
  /\ lobby' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyEpoch, commitCount>>

  /\ lobbyEpoch = epoch
  /\ commitCount[epoch] = 0

\* delay, or duplicate them, so a request stamped with an old epoch can
\* still be lying around after a reconfiguration has advanced the epoch.

    /\ inFlight = {}
    /\ commitLog = {}

\* committed and has no request already outstanding in this epoch.
SendRequest(u) ==
    /\ u \notin committed
    /\ ~ \E m \in inFlight : m.unit = u /\ m.epoch = epoch
    /\ inFlight' = inFlight \cup {[unit |-> u, epoch |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, committed, commitLog, seq>>

\* epoch and its unit has not already been irreversibly issued. Each commit
\* gets a fresh seq number so a duplicate commit of the same unit can never
\* be masked away by set deduplication in the log.

    /\ m \in inFlight
    /\ m.epoch = epoch
    /\ m.unit \notin committed
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {m.unit}
    /\ commitLog' = commitLog \cup {[unit |-> m.unit, seq |-> seq]}
    /\ seq' = seq + 1
    /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* acted upon, since reconfiguration has already fenced it off.

    /\ m.epoch < epoch
    /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, committed, commitLog, seq>>

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the coordinator advances the epoch,
\* fencing off any request still labeled with an older epoch.

    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, inFlight, commitLog, seq>>

    \/ \E m \in inFlight : CommitIssue(m)
    \/ \E m \in inFlight : DropStale(m)

\* once, even though its issuance request may be duplicated, delayed, or
\* reordered across an epoch change. Checked against the append-only log
\* rather than the guard set, so a broken guard would be caught.

    \A u \in Units : Cardinality({c \in commitLog : c.unit = u}) <= 1

A blood-bank inventory system tracks units of blood that may each be issued
to a patient exactly once, since an issued unit is irreversibly consumed and
cannot be recalled. Issuance is driven by an epoch-numbered reconfiguration
protocol: a coordinator stamps every issuance request with the current epoch
number before broadcasting it, and periodically advances the epoch to fence
off stale requests after a reconfiguration event. The underlying network can
reorder, delay, or leave duplicate copies of these requests in flight, so a
request stamped with an old epoch may still be sitting around after the
epoch has moved on. The protocol only honors (commits) a request whose epoch
stamp matches the current epoch and whose unit has not already been
committed; anything stamped with a stale epoch is dropped instead of being
acted upon. Every commit is recorded with a fresh, unique sequence number in
an append-only log so that even a same-epoch or cross-epoch duplicate
commit would show up as two distinct log entries for the same unit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No blood unit is ever irreversibly issued (committed) more than once, despite request duplication, delay, or reordering across epoch changes.

---- MODULE W4Od1m5p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxCapacity, Quorum, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES capacity, epoch, authorized, votes, granted, pending

vars == <<capacity, epoch, authorized, votes, granted, pending>>

\* Runway clearances are decided by quorum vote among currently authorized
\* controllers; a vote only counts if cast in the current epoch. Reconfigure
\* models a runtime capacity/roster change: it starts a new epoch and forces
\* any active clearances to be revoked and re-certified.

TypeOK ==
  /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCapacity
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ authorized \subseteq Controllers
  /\ votes \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ granted \in 0..MaxCapacity
  /\ pending \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ capacity = MaxCapacity
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ authorized = Controllers
  /\ votes = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
  /\ granted = 0
  /\ pending = FALSE

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \E newCap \in 0..MaxCapacity, newAuth \in (SUBSET Controllers) \ {{}} :
       /\ capacity' = newCap
       /\ authorized' = newAuth
       /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
       /\ granted' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, pending>>

NewRequest ==
  /\ pending = FALSE
  /\ pending' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, epoch, authorized, votes, granted>>

Vote(c) ==
  /\ pending = TRUE
  /\ c \in authorized
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, epoch, authorized, granted, pending>>

VoteStep == \E c \in Controllers : Vote(c)

Grant ==
  /\ pending = TRUE
  /\ granted < capacity
  /\ \E Q \in SUBSET authorized :
       /\ Cardinality(Q) >= Quorum
       /\ \A c \in Q : votes[c] = epoch
  /\ granted' = granted + 1
  /\ pending' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, epoch, authorized, votes>>

Reject ==
  /\ pending = TRUE
  /\ pending' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, epoch, authorized, votes, granted>>

Depart ==
  /\ granted > 0
  /\ granted' = granted - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, epoch, authorized, votes, pending>>

Next == Reconfigure \/ NewRequest \/ VoteStep \/ Grant \/ Reject \/ Depart

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(VoteStep) /\ WF_vars(Grant) /\ WF_vars(Reject)

\* Safety: an active clearance must always be traceable to a quorum of
\* controllers that are currently authorized and voted in the current epoch
\* -- no unauthorized or stale (superseded-epoch) participant can back it.
QuorumCertified ==
  granted > 0 =>
    \E Q \in SUBSET authorized :
      /\ Cardinality(Q) >= Quorum
      /\ \A c \in Q : votes[c] = epoch

\* Liveness: every open clearance request is eventually resolved.
EventuallyResolved == pending ~> ~pending

====

PROPERTY EventuallyResolved

nl:
This specification models an air-traffic runway allocator where clearance requests are decided by quorum vote among a dynamically certified set of controllers. A controller can only cast a valid vote while it holds current authorization, and a vote only counts toward a clearance decision if it was cast in the controller's current certification epoch; whenever the runway's capacity or the authorized-controller roster changes at runtime (a reconfiguration), a new epoch begins and any previously active clearances are revoked, requiring re-certification against the new roster and epoch before further clearances can be granted. Vote records persist as history, so a controller who is later dropped from the authorized set, or whose vote was cast in an epoch that has since been superseded, cannot have that stale vote silently contribute to a fresh clearance decision. Clearance requests arrive one at a time and are eventually either granted, if a fresh quorum of currently authorized controllers backs them and capacity allows, or rejected.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A runway clearance may be active only if it is backed by a quorum of controllers that are currently authorized and cast their certifying vote in the current epoch, never a stale or unauthorized participant.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every open clearance request is eventually resolved, either granted or rejected.

---- MODULE W4Od5m4p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Players, MaxQueue, MaxSeq

VARIABLES queue, value, version, nextSeq, log, backpressure

\* queue holds in-flight lobby-update messages; it may be reordered in transit
\* to model an unreliable, backpressured delivery channel.
\* version/log record which sequence numbers have actually been committed to
\* the shared record "value", so a reordered stale message can be detected
\* and discarded instead of clobbering a newer already-applied update.

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq([seq: 1..MaxSeq, val: Players])
  /\ value \in Players
  /\ version \in 0..MaxSeq
  /\ nextSeq \in 1..(MaxSeq + 1)
  /\ log \in Seq(1..MaxSeq)
  /\ backpressure \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ value \in Players
  /\ version = 0
  /\ nextSeq = 1
  /\ log = <<>>
  /\ backpressure = FALSE

\* Producer enqueues a fresh update, tagging it with the next sequence number,
\* as long as the bounded queue still has room.
Produce ==
  /\ nextSeq <= MaxSeq
  /\ Len(queue) < MaxQueue
  /\ \E p \in Players :
       queue' = Append(queue, [seq |-> nextSeq, val |-> p])
  /\ nextSeq' = nextSeq + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<value, version, log, backpressure>>

\* Backpressure: queue is saturated, so the attempted update is dropped and
\* flagged rather than silently blocking forever.
RejectProduce ==
  /\ nextSeq <= MaxSeq
  /\ Len(queue) = MaxQueue
  /\ backpressure' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, value, version, nextSeq, log>>

\* The transport may reorder any two adjacent in-flight messages.
Reorder ==
  /\ Len(queue) >= 2
  /\ \E i \in 1..(Len(queue) - 1) :
       queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![i] = queue[i + 1], ![i + 1] = queue[i]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<value, version, nextSeq, log, backpressure>>

\* Consumer dequeues the head message. A newer message (higher sequence
\* number than what is currently committed) is applied to the shared record;
\* a stale one (reordered to the front too late) is discarded, never
\* overwriting the newer value already in place.
Apply ==
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ LET m == Head(queue) IN
       IF m.seq > version
       THEN /\ value' = m.val
            /\ version' = m.seq
            /\ log' = Append(log, m.seq)
       ELSE /\ value' = value
            /\ version' = version
            /\ log' = log
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<nextSeq, backpressure>>

Next == Produce \/ RejectProduce \/ Reorder \/ Apply

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<queue, value, version, nextSeq, log, backpressure>>

\* No lost updates: the committed log of applied sequence numbers is always
\* strictly increasing, and version always matches its last entry, so a
\* reordered stale message can never overwrite a newer committed update.
SafetyInv ==
  /\ (Len(log) > 0 => version = log[Len(log)])
  /\ \A i \in 1..(Len(log) - 1) : log[i] < log[i + 1]

====

CONSTANTS
  Players = {p1, p2}
  MaxQueue = 2
  MaxSeq = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SafetyInv

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In a multiplayer game lobby matchmaker, clients send updates about the lobby's
shared record (for example, "who currently holds the host slot") through a
bounded work queue that applies backpressure once it is full: the matchmaker
either accepts a new update into the queue or, if the queue is saturated,
drops the attempt and flags that backpressure occurred. Each update carries
a monotonically increasing sequence number assigned when it was produced.
Because the transport between producer and consumer can reorder in-flight
messages, updates may arrive at the front of the queue out of the order in
which they were produced. The consumer must therefore never let a
stale (lower sequence number) update silently overwrite the effect of a
newer one that has already been applied to the shared record; it detects and
discards stale updates instead of applying them.

SAFETY PROPERTY: once the shared lobby record has been updated by a message
with sequence number N, no update with a sequence number <= N is ever applied
afterward, so the record's committed-update history is always strictly
increasing in sequence number despite arbitrary reordering of queued messages.

---- MODULE W4Od10m1p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Integers

CONSTANTS NumNodes, TotalPermits, MaxOverrides

ASSUME NumNodes \in Nat /\ NumNodes > 1
ASSUME TotalPermits \in Nat
ASSUME MaxOverrides \in Nat

Nodes == 0..(NumNodes - 1)
Home == 0

VARIABLES pos, permits, carried, adminActive, overrideBudget

vars == <<pos, permits, carried, adminActive, overrideBudget>>

\* Recursive helper: sums the permits parked at every signalling block on the ring.
RECURSIVE SumFrom(_)
SumFrom(i) == IF i >= NumNodes THEN 0 ELSE permits[i] + SumFrom(i + 1)

TypeOK ==
  /\ pos \in Nodes
  /\ permits \in [Nodes -> 0..TotalPermits]
  /\ carried \in 0..TotalPermits
  /\ adminActive \in BOOLEAN
  /\ overrideBudget \in 0..MaxOverrides

\* SAFETY: permits held at blocks plus the permit carried by the mobile grant token
\* must always sum to the fixed total -- the admin override may relocate permits or
\* the token itself, but it can never create or destroy a permit.
Conservation == (SumFrom(0) + carried) = TotalPermits

Init ==
  /\ pos = 1
  /\ permits = [n \in Nodes |-> IF n = 1 THEN TotalPermits ELSE 0]
  /\ carried = 0
  /\ adminActive = FALSE
  /\ overrideBudget = MaxOverrides

\* Advance: the grant token hands off to the next block in normal ring order.
Advance ==
  /\ pos' = (pos + 1) % NumNodes
  /\ UNCHANGED <<permits, carried, overrideBudget>>
  /\ adminActive' = FALSE

\* Deposit: the block holding the grant token absorbs one permit carried by the token.
Deposit ==
  /\ carried > 0
  /\ permits' = [permits EXCEPT ![pos] = @ + 1]
  /\ carried' = carried - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, overrideBudget>>
  /\ adminActive' = FALSE

\* Collect: the block holding the grant token releases one permit onto the token.
Collect ==
  /\ permits[pos] > 0
  /\ permits' = [permits EXCEPT ![pos] = @ - 1]
  /\ carried' = carried + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, overrideBudget>>
  /\ adminActive' = FALSE

\* AdminJump: the privileged override relocates the token out of ring order; a limited,
\* metered emergency power that is exhausted after MaxOverrides uses.
AdminJump ==
  /\ overrideBudget > 0
  /\ \E n \in Nodes : pos' = n
  /\ overrideBudget' = overrideBudget - 1
  /\ adminActive' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<permits, carried>>

\* AdminTransfer: the override reassigns one permit directly between two blocks,
\* bypassing the token mechanism, still spending from the same metered budget.
AdminTransfer ==
  /\ overrideBudget > 0
  /\ \E a, b \in Nodes :
       /\ a # b
       /\ permits[a] > 0
       /\ permits' = [permits EXCEPT ![a] = @ - 1, ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ overrideBudget' = overrideBudget - 1
  /\ adminActive' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, carried>>

Next == Advance \/ Deposit \/ Collect \/ AdminJump \/ AdminTransfer

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Advance) /\ WF_vars(Deposit) /\ WF_vars(Collect)

\* LIVENESS: once the metered admin override is exhausted, ordinary ring rotation
\* resumes and the grant token keeps coming home to block 0 infinitely often.
ReturnsHome == []<>(pos = Home)

====

CONSTANTS
  NumNodes = 3
  TotalPermits = 2
  MaxOverrides = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT Conservation

PROPERTY ReturnsHome

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
This spec models a subway signalling block system arranged as a ring of track blocks.
A single mobile "grant" token circulates the ring, normally handing off from one block
to the next in fixed order, and each block can accept a signalling permit from the
token (Deposit) or release one back onto the token (Collect). The total number of
permits circulating the ring -- whether parked at a block or currently carried by the
grant token -- is a fixed conserved quantity representing the total signalling capacity
of the line. A privileged admin override exists for emergencies: it can relocate the
grant token to any block out of normal ring order, or reassign a permit directly
between two blocks, bypassing the token mechanism entirely -- but this override is
metered (a small fixed budget of uses) and, crucially, it never creates or destroys a
permit, only moves them. Once the admin's override budget is exhausted, ordinary ring
rotation resumes unimpeded, and fairness on the rotation action guarantees the grant
token keeps returning to the designated home block.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of permits parked at every block plus the permit (if any) carried by the mobile grant token always equals the fixed total number of permits in circulation, even across admin overrides.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The grant token eventually and infinitely often returns to the designated home block (block 0), i.e. normal ring rotation is not permanently starved out by the metered admin override.

---- MODULE W4Od10m9p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, Slots, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, holds, network, reconfiguring

Message == [slot: Slots, train: Trains, epoch: 0..MaxEpoch]
Hold    == [slot: Slots, train: Trains, epoch: 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ holds \subseteq Hold
  /\ network \subseteq Message
  /\ reconfiguring \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ holds = {}
  /\ network = {}
  /\ reconfiguring = FALSE

\* Controller begins reconfiguring: freezes new assignment requests
BeginReconfigure ==
  /\ ~reconfiguring
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ reconfiguring' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holds, network>>

\* Reconfiguration completes: epoch advances, prior holds are invalidated
FinishReconfigure ==
  /\ reconfiguring
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ holds' = {}
  /\ reconfiguring' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED network

\* Controller sends an assignment request tagged with the current epoch
SendAssign(t, s) ==
  /\ ~reconfiguring
  /\ network' = network \cup {[slot |-> s, train |-> t, epoch |-> epoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holds, reconfiguring>>

\* Deliver a (possibly reordered/stale) message; a message tagged with a
\* stale epoch is simply discarded, so reordering can never grant a slot
\* that conflicts with a later assignment.
Deliver(m) ==
  /\ m \in network
  /\ network' = network \ {m}
  /\ IF /\ m.epoch = epoch
        /\ ~reconfiguring
        /\ ~ \E h \in holds : h.slot = m.slot
       THEN holds' = holds \cup {[slot |-> m.slot, train |-> m.train, epoch |-> epoch]}
       ELSE holds' = holds
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, reconfiguring>>

\* A train releases a held slot, freeing it for future reassignment
Release(s) ==
  /\ \E h \in holds : h.slot = s
  /\ holds' = { h \in holds : h.slot # s }
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, network, reconfiguring>>

Next ==
  \/ BeginReconfigure
  \/ FinishReconfigure
  \/ \E t \in Trains, s \in Slots : SendAssign(t, s)
  \/ \E m \in network : Deliver(m)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Release(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, holds, network, reconfiguring>>

\* Safety: each slot has at most one owning train, and that owner is tied
\* to a single reconfiguration epoch -- no double allocation of a slot.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A h1, h2 \in holds :
    (h1.slot = h2.slot) => (h1.train = h2.train /\ h1.epoch = h2.epoch)

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway signalling block system divides track into discrete signalling
slots that trains must occupy exclusively to avoid collisions. A central
controller assigns slots to trains, and periodically performs an epoch
numbered reconfiguration (e.g. when a section is re-partitioned or a
signal box takes over from another). Every assignment request the
controller sends is tagged with the epoch that was current when it was
issued. The network delivering these requests to trains can reorder or
delay them arbitrarily, so a request issued before a reconfiguration may
arrive after the epoch has already advanced. The controller guards
against this by having trains (and the simulated delivery step) reject
any request whose tagged epoch does not match the epoch in force at
delivery time, and by clearing all outstanding slot holds whenever a
reconfiguration completes, so stale, reordered requests can never grant
a slot that conflicts with a fresh assignment made under a later epoch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No signalling slot is ever simultaneously held by two
different trains (or under two different epochs), even though
assignment request messages may be delivered out of order.

---- MODULE W4Od8m9p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS TotalSeats, StartReqA, StartReqB, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES pool, seatedA, seatedB, reqA, reqB, epoch

vars == <<pool, seatedA, seatedB, reqA, reqB, epoch>>

\* Epoch parity assigns exclusive access to the shared seat pool: even epochs
\* belong to instance A, odd epochs belong to instance B. Reconfigure is the
\* epoch-guarded mechanism that hands pool access to the other instance.
InstanceATurn == epoch % 2 = 0
InstanceBTurn == epoch % 2 = 1

Init ==
  /\ pool = TotalSeats
  /\ seatedA = 0
  /\ seatedB = 0
  /\ reqA = StartReqA
  /\ reqB = StartReqB
  /\ epoch = 0

SeatA ==
  /\ InstanceATurn
  /\ reqA > 0
  /\ pool > 0
  /\ pool' = pool - 1
  /\ seatedA' = seatedA + 1
  /\ reqA' = reqA - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seatedB, reqB, epoch>>

SeatB ==
  /\ InstanceBTurn
  /\ reqB > 0
  /\ pool > 0
  /\ pool' = pool - 1
  /\ seatedB' = seatedB + 1
  /\ reqB' = reqB - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seatedA, reqA, epoch>>

\* A pending request is rejected only when it is that instance's turn and the
\* shared pool is exhausted -- so no request can wait forever.
RejectA ==
  /\ InstanceATurn
  /\ reqA > 0
  /\ pool = 0
  /\ reqA' = reqA - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, seatedA, seatedB, reqB, epoch>>

RejectB ==
  /\ InstanceBTurn
  /\ reqB > 0
  /\ pool = 0
  /\ reqB' = reqB - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, seatedA, seatedB, reqA, epoch>>

\* Reconfiguration only hands access to the other instance once the current
\* holder's pending requests are all resolved -- it cannot pre-empt a turn.
Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ InstanceATurn => reqA = 0
  /\ InstanceBTurn => reqB = 0
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, seatedA, seatedB, reqA, reqB>>

\* A seated student may drop the course, returning the seat to the shared
\* pool. Seats only ever move between pool and seated counts, never vanish.
DropA ==
  /\ seatedA > 0
  /\ seatedA' = seatedA - 1
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seatedB, reqA, reqB, epoch>>

DropB ==
  /\ seatedB > 0
  /\ seatedB' = seatedB - 1
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seatedA, reqA, reqB, epoch>>

Next == SeatA \/ SeatB \/ RejectA \/ RejectB \/ Reconfigure \/ DropA \/ DropB

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
           /\ WF_vars(SeatA) /\ WF_vars(SeatB)
           /\ WF_vars(RejectA) /\ WF_vars(RejectB)
           /\ WF_vars(Reconfigure)

\* Safety: total seats in the shared pool plus both instances' seated
\* students is conserved -- reconfiguration only moves seats, never creates
\* or destroys them.
SeatConservation == pool + seatedA + seatedB = TotalSeats

\* Liveness: every pending registration request at either instance is
\* eventually resolved -- seated or rejected -- never left pending forever.
AllRequestsResolved == <>(reqA = 0 /\ reqB = 0)

This spec models a university course-registration system built from two independent registration instances, A and B, that share a single pool of course seats. Access to the shared pool is governed by an epoch-numbered reconfiguration mechanism: the epoch's parity grants exclusive access to the pool to one instance at a time, and a Reconfigure action advances the epoch to hand access over to the other instance. Seats only ever move between the shared pool and the two instances' seated counts -- they are never created or destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od2m0p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Cap, VMax

VARIABLES occA, occB, verA, verB, ver

\* occA/occB: robots currently holding a dock slot claimed by fleet instance A / B
\* verA/verB: the shared pool version each instance last read when starting a reservation attempt
\* ver: shared version counter, bumped on every successful commit or release (the CAS token)

TypeOK ==
    /\ occA \in 0..Cap
    /\ occB \in 0..Cap
    /\ verA \in ({-1} \cup 0..VMax)
    /\ verB \in ({-1} \cup 0..VMax)
    /\ ver \in 0..VMax

Init ==
    /\ occA = 0
    /\ occB = 0
    /\ verA = -1
    /\ verB = -1
    /\ ver = 0

StartA ==
    /\ verA = -1
    /\ occA + occB < Cap
    /\ verA' = ver
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, occB, verB, ver>>

\* CommitA succeeds only if the pool version is unchanged since StartA's read (optimistic check);
\* otherwise it aborts and clears verA so instance A retries with a fresh read next time
CommitA ==
    /\ verA # -1
    /\ IF verA = ver /\ ver < VMax
       THEN /\ occA' = occA + 1
            /\ ver' = ver + 1
            /\ verA' = -1
       ELSE /\ verA' = -1
            /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, ver>>
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occB, verB>>

ReleaseA ==
    /\ occA > 0
    /\ ver < VMax
    /\ occA' = occA - 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occB, verA, verB>>

StartB ==
    /\ verB = -1
    /\ occA + occB < Cap
    /\ verB' = ver
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, occB, verA, ver>>

\* CommitB mirrors CommitA: only commits if no other commit slipped in since its read
CommitB ==
    /\ verB # -1
    /\ IF verB = ver /\ ver < VMax
       THEN /\ occB' = occB + 1
            /\ ver' = ver + 1
            /\ verB' = -1
       ELSE /\ verB' = -1
            /\ UNCHANGED <<occB, ver>>
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, verA>>

ReleaseB ==
    /\ occB > 0
    /\ ver < VMax
    /\ occB' = occB - 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, verA, verB>>

Next == StartA \/ CommitA \/ ReleaseA \/ StartB \/ CommitB \/ ReleaseB

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<occA, occB, verA, verB, ver>>

\* Safety: combined occupancy from both fleet instances must never exceed the shared pool's capacity
CapacityOK == occA + occB <= Cap

Robots also depart, releasing their dock slot back to the shared pool. Because both instances draw from the same pool, the correctness of the whole fleet depends on their optimistic commits never overshooting the shared limit together.

---- MODULE W4Od6m8p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Capacity

\* Two boarding candidates share one cabin of the given Capacity.
Passengers == {"p1", "p2"}

VARIABLES status, crashed, occupancy, coarseLock, fineLock

vars == <<status, crashed, occupancy, coarseLock, fineLock>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ status \in [Passengers -> {"idle", "called", "waiting", "boarding", "boarded"}]
  /\ crashed \in [Passengers -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ occupancy \in 0..Capacity
  /\ coarseLock \in BOOLEAN
  /\ fineLock \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ status = [p \in Passengers |-> "idle"]
  /\ crashed = [p \in Passengers |-> FALSE]
  /\ occupancy = 0
  /\ coarseLock = FALSE
  /\ fineLock = FALSE

\* Coarse lock: only one passenger may register a floor call at a time.
CallFloor(p) ==
  /\ status[p] = "idle"
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ ~coarseLock
  /\ coarseLock' = TRUE
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "called"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, occupancy, fineLock>>

ReleaseCoarse(p) ==
  /\ status[p] = "called"
  /\ coarseLock' = FALSE
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "waiting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, occupancy, fineLock>>

\* Fine lock: the finer-grained gate that actually admits a passenger into
\* the cabin, rechecking capacity right at the point of boarding.
AcquireFine(p) ==
  /\ status[p] = "waiting"
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ ~fineLock
  /\ occupancy < Capacity
  /\ fineLock' = TRUE
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "boarding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, occupancy, coarseLock>>

ReleaseFine(p) ==
  /\ status[p] = "boarding"
  /\ fineLock' = FALSE
  /\ occupancy' = occupancy + 1
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "boarded"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, coarseLock>>

ExitCabin(p) ==
  /\ status[p] = "boarded"
  /\ occupancy' = occupancy - 1
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, coarseLock, fineLock>>

\* Twist: at most one passenger ever crashes silently, and only while it
\* holds no lock, so its stall cannot wedge the other passenger's progress.
Crash(p) ==
  /\ status[p] \in {"idle", "waiting"}
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ \A q \in Passengers : ~crashed[q]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, occupancy, coarseLock, fineLock>>

Next ==
  \E p \in Passengers :
    \/ CallFloor(p)
    \/ ReleaseCoarse(p)
    \/ AcquireFine(p)
    \/ ReleaseFine(p)
    \/ ExitCabin(p)
    \/ Crash(p)

\* Contended lock-acquisition steps need strong fairness so a passenger
\* cannot be starved forever by the other repeatedly winning the race;
\* the uncontended release/exit steps only need weak fairness.
Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(CallFloor("p1"))     /\ SF_vars(CallFloor("p2"))
  /\ WF_vars(ReleaseCoarse("p1")) /\ WF_vars(ReleaseCoarse("p2"))
  /\ SF_vars(AcquireFine("p1"))   /\ SF_vars(AcquireFine("p2"))
  /\ WF_vars(ReleaseFine("p1"))   /\ WF_vars(ReleaseFine("p2"))
  /\ WF_vars(ExitCabin("p1"))     /\ WF_vars(ExitCabin("p2"))

\* SAFETY: cabin occupancy is exactly the count of boarded passengers and
\* never exceeds the cabin's fixed capacity.
CapacityInvariant ==
  LET boarded == {p \in Passengers : status[p] = "boarded"} IN
    /\ occupancy = Cardinality(boarded)
    /\ Cardinality(boarded) <= Capacity

RequestPending(p) == status[p] \in {"called", "waiting", "boarding"}
Served(p) == status[p] = "boarded"

\* LIVENESS: every non-crashed passenger's floor-call request is eventually
\* boarded (or explicitly abandoned by a silent crash).
RequestsEventuallyServed ==
  \A p \in Passengers : RequestPending(p) ~> (Served(p) \/ crashed[p])

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityInvariant
PROPERTY RequestsEventuallyServed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In a skyscraper's elevator bank, two passengers, p1 and p2, share a single cabin of fixed
Capacity. Boarding is admitted through a hierarchical pair of locks: a coarse lock guards
the floor-call step (only one passenger may register a call at a time), and after that
lock is released the passenger waits for a finer-grained lock that guards the actual
cabin-boarding step, rechecking the cabin's remaining capacity right at the moment of
admission. Once boarded, a passenger eventually exits, freeing the cabin for others. As a
twist, at most one of the two passengers may crash silently at any point while it holds
neither lock (idle or already waiting for a boarding slot); a crashed passenger's own
request simply stalls forever, but it never holds a lock when it crashes, so it cannot
block the other passenger's boarding cycle.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of passengers currently in the cabin never exceeds the cabin's fixed capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every non-crashed passenger's pending floor-call request is eventually served (boarded), unless it is abandoned by a silent crash.

---- MODULE W4Od8m4p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Capacity, QueueCap

VARIABLES queue, inProgress, enrolled, rejected, submitted

vars == <<queue, inProgress, enrolled, rejected, submitted>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Students)
    /\ inProgress \subseteq Students
    /\ enrolled \subseteq Students
    /\ rejected \subseteq Students
    /\ submitted \subseteq Students

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ inProgress = {}
    /\ enrolled = {}
    /\ rejected = {}
    /\ submitted = {}

\* A new registration request is enqueued only while there is room in the
\* bounded queue.
Submit(s) ==
    /\ s \notin submitted
    /\ Len(queue) < QueueCap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, s)
    /\ submitted' = submitted \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inProgress, enrolled, rejected>>

\* Backpressure: once the queue is at capacity, a new request is dropped
\* instead of being admitted.
Backpressure(s) ==
    /\ s \notin submitted
    /\ Len(queue) >= QueueCap
    /\ rejected' = rejected \cup {s}
    /\ submitted' = submitted \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inProgress, enrolled>>

\* A worker dequeues the head of the queue, reserving a seat for it only if
\* capacity allows. The request now occupies a reserved slot until it
\* completes or the student withdraws.
StartProcessing ==
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ Cardinality(enrolled) + Cardinality(inProgress) < Capacity
    /\ inProgress' = inProgress \cup {Head(queue)}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, rejected, submitted>>

\* A request in progress may complete at any time; it can also remain in
\* progress for arbitrarily many steps (slow but never failed).
CompleteRegistration(s) ==
    /\ s \in inProgress
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {s}
    /\ inProgress' = inProgress \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, rejected, submitted>>

\* An enrolled student may withdraw, freeing their seat.
Withdraw(s) ==
    /\ s \in enrolled
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inProgress, rejected, submitted>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students : Submit(s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Backpressure(s)
    \/ StartProcessing
    \/ \E s \in Students : CompleteRegistration(s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Withdraw(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: reserved-or-enrolled seats never exceed course capacity, and the
\* pending queue never grows past its bounded depth.
CapacityInvariant ==
    /\ Cardinality(enrolled) + Cardinality(inProgress) <= Capacity
    /\ Len(queue) <= QueueCap

either eventually completes and becomes enrolled, or stays pending indefinitely. Enrolled students
may later withdraw, freeing a seat for someone else.

---- MODULE W4Od16m2p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Requests, MinCapacity, MaxCapacity, InitialCapacity

VARIABLES status, reserved, committed, capacity

vars == <<status, reserved, committed, capacity>>

\* Every request asks for one unit of a prescription; keeps the model tiny
\* while still exercising the two-phase commit / capacity mechanism.
Qty == [r \in Requests |-> 1]

\* Two-phase commit: Prepare tentatively reserves capacity for a request,
\* Commit finalizes the dispense against a fresh capacity check, Abort releases
\* the reservation. Capacity itself may change at runtime (the twist), but
\* never below what has already been physically dispensed (committed).

TypeOK ==
  /\ status \in [Requests -> {"idle", "prepared", "committed", "aborted"}]
  /\ reserved \in Nat
  /\ committed \in Nat
  /\ capacity \in MinCapacity..MaxCapacity

Init ==
  /\ status = [r \in Requests |-> "idle"]
  /\ reserved = 0
  /\ committed = 0
  /\ capacity = InitialCapacity

Prepare(r) ==
  /\ status[r] = "idle"
  /\ reserved + committed + Qty[r] <= capacity
  /\ reserved' = reserved + Qty[r]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![r] = "prepared"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, capacity>>

\* Commit re-checks capacity at dispense time since capacity may have shrunk
\* since the matching Prepare.
Commit(r) ==
  /\ status[r] = "prepared"
  /\ committed + Qty[r] <= capacity
  /\ committed' = committed + Qty[r]
  /\ reserved' = reserved - Qty[r]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![r] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

Abort(r) ==
  /\ status[r] = "prepared"
  /\ reserved' = reserved - Qty[r]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![r] = "aborted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, capacity>>

\* Runtime capacity change: never allowed to drop below already-dispensed quantity.
ChangeCapacity ==
  /\ \E newCap \in MinCapacity..MaxCapacity:
       /\ newCap >= committed
       /\ capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, reserved, committed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Requests: Prepare(r)
  \/ \E r \in Requests: Commit(r)
  \/ \E r \in Requests: Abort(r)
  \/ ChangeCapacity

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Requests: Prepare(r))
  /\ WF_vars(\E r \in Requests: Commit(r) \/ Abort(r))
  /\ WF_vars(ChangeCapacity)

\* SAFETY: dispensed (committed) quantity never exceeds current capacity.
CapacityNotExceeded == committed <= capacity

\* LIVENESS: every request that is prepared eventually resolves (commit or abort).
EventualResolution ==
  \A r \in Requests: (status[r] = "prepared") ~> (status[r] \in {"committed", "aborted"})

====

nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser processes prescription-fill requests against a shared
dispensing capacity using a two-phase commit protocol across participants. In the prepare
phase, a request tentatively reserves the quantity it needs against the current capacity
(a "vote" that there is room). In the commit phase, the reservation is turned into an
actual dispense only after re-checking capacity, since the dispenser's capacity can be
adjusted at runtime (e.g. a shift change, restock, or equipment failure) between the
prepare and commit steps; if capacity has shrunk too far, the request is aborted instead
and its reservation released. Capacity may never be lowered below the quantity that has
already been physically dispensed. The system must guarantee both that the pharmacy never
dispenses more than its declared capacity, and that no prescription request is left stuck
forever in the tentative "prepared" state.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total quantity actually committed (dispensed) never exceeds the current dispensing capacity, even as that capacity changes at runtime.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every prescription request that reaches the prepared phase eventually resolves, either committing or aborting, and never stalls in the prepared state forever.

---- MODULE W4Od11m4p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS JOBS, Capacity, PrintTime

VARIABLES queue, printing, progress, doneSet, submitted

\* queue is the FIFO spooler holding jobs waiting for the printer
\* printing holds at most one job currently on the (possibly slow) printer
\* progress counts printer ticks so a slow job is never lost or duplicated
\* doneSet holds jobs the printer has finished; submitted gates backpressure

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(JOBS)
  /\ printing \in JOBS \union {"empty"}
  /\ progress \in 0..PrintTime
  /\ doneSet \subseteq JOBS
  /\ submitted \subseteq JOBS

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ printing = "empty"
  /\ progress = 0
  /\ doneSet = {}
  /\ submitted = {}

InQueueSet == {queue[i] : i \in DOMAIN queue}
InPrinterSet == IF printing = "empty" THEN {} ELSE {printing}

Submit(j) ==
  /\ j \notin submitted
  /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, j)
  /\ submitted' = submitted \union {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<printing, progress, doneSet>>

StartPrint ==
  /\ printing = "empty"
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ printing' = Head(queue)
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ progress' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<doneSet, submitted>>

\* the printer may be slow: it can tick many times before finishing,
\* but the in-flight job stays put the whole time, never dropped
SlowStep ==
  /\ printing # "empty"
  /\ progress < PrintTime
  /\ progress' = progress + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, printing, doneSet, submitted>>

FinishPrint ==
  /\ printing # "empty"
  /\ progress = PrintTime
  /\ doneSet' = doneSet \union {printing}
  /\ printing' = "empty"
  /\ progress' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, submitted>>

Next ==
  \/ \E j \in JOBS : Submit(j)
  \/ StartPrint
  \/ SlowStep
  \/ FinishPrint

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<queue, printing, progress, doneSet, submitted>>

\* Conservation: every submitted job sits in exactly one of the three
\* places (queued, on the printer, done) and nothing else ever appears -
\* a job is never created out of thin air nor destroyed while in flight
Conservation ==
  /\ InQueueSet \cap InPrinterSet = {}
  /\ InQueueSet \cap doneSet = {}
  /\ InPrinterSet \cap doneSet = {}
  /\ (InQueueSet \union InPrinterSet \union doneSet) = submitted

====

CONSTANTS
  JOBS = {j1, j2, j3}
  Capacity = 2
  PrintTime = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conservation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A small print shop runs a spooler in front of a single printer. Customers submit print jobs into a bounded work queue; when the queue is full, the shop applies backpressure and refuses new submissions until space frees up. The printer pulls one job at a time off the front of the queue and works on it. The printer can be slow - it may need several ticks to finish a job - but it is never assumed to fail or crash; a job it is working on simply sits in progress, tick after tick, until it completes. Once finished, the job moves to the completed pile. At every point, each job that has ever been submitted must be accounted for in exactly one place: still queued, currently on the (possibly slow) printer, or finished, with no job ever appearing twice or vanishing.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every job that has been submitted is present in exactly one of the queue, the printer, or the done pile, and no job appears in more than one place or in none.

---- MODULE W4Od3m3p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS P1, P2, E1, E2, MaxTerm, MinCap, MaxCap, InitLeader

Participants == {P1, P2}
Entries == {E1, E2}

VARIABLES term, leaderLog, believed, status, committedBy, capacity

vars == <<term, leaderLog, believed, status, committedBy, capacity>>

\* leaderLog[t] records the participant authorized to commit entries during term t;
\* it is set once at election time and never revised, giving each term one authority.
Init ==
  /\ term = 1
  /\ leaderLog = [t \in 1..MaxTerm |-> IF t = 1 THEN InitLeader ELSE "None"]
  /\ believed = [p \in Participants |-> 1]
  /\ status = [e \in Entries |-> "unsubmitted"]
  /\ committedBy = [e \in Entries |-> [by |-> "None", term |-> 0]]
  /\ capacity = MinCap

\* Failover advances the term and installs a new leader; other participants may
\* remain unaware (stale) of the change until they explicitly resync belief.
Failover ==
  \E p \in Participants :
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leaderLog' = [leaderLog EXCEPT ![term + 1] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<believed, status, committedBy, capacity>>

SyncBelief(p) ==
  /\ believed[p] < term
  /\ believed' = [believed EXCEPT ![p] = term]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderLog, status, committedBy, capacity>>

\* Admission into the batch window is capped by the runtime-adjustable capacity.
Submit(e) ==
  /\ status[e] = "unsubmitted"
  /\ Cardinality({x \in Entries : status[x] = "pending"}) < capacity
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![e] = "pending"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderLog, believed, committedBy, capacity>>

\* Only the participant currently recorded as leader for the live term, who also
\* knows it, may commit a pending settlement entry -- the authorization guard.
CommitEntry(e) ==
  \E p \in Participants :
    /\ status[e] = "pending"
    /\ leaderLog[term] = p
    /\ believed[p] = term
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![e] = "committed"]
    /\ committedBy' = [committedBy EXCEPT ![e] = [by |-> p, term |-> term]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderLog, believed, capacity>>

\* A participant still acting on an outdated term (its belief lags the live
\* term) has any pending entry it touches discarded rather than committed.
DiscardStale(e) ==
  \E p \in Participants :
    /\ status[e] = "pending"
    /\ believed[p] < term
    /\ leaderLog[believed[p]] = p
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![e] = "discarded"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderLog, believed, committedBy, capacity>>

AdjustCapacity ==
  \E c \in MinCap..MaxCap :
    /\ c # capacity
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderLog, believed, status, committedBy>>

Next ==
  \/ Failover
  \/ SyncBelief(P1) \/ SyncBelief(P2)
  \/ Submit(E1) \/ Submit(E2)
  \/ CommitEntry(E1) \/ CommitEntry(E2)
  \/ DiscardStale(E1) \/ DiscardStale(E2)
  \/ AdjustCapacity

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Submit(E1)) /\ WF_vars(Submit(E2))
  /\ WF_vars(CommitEntry(E1)) /\ WF_vars(CommitEntry(E2))
  /\ WF_vars(DiscardStale(E1)) /\ WF_vars(DiscardStale(E2))
  /\ WF_vars(SyncBelief(P1)) /\ WF_vars(SyncBelief(P2))

\* Safety: a committed entry's recorded committer must equal the leader that
\* was actually authorized for the term stamped on that commit -- no stale or
\* unauthorized participant's commit is ever recognized as valid.
NoStaleCommit ==
  \A e \in Entries :
    status[e] = "committed" => leaderLog[committedBy[e].term] = committedBy[e].by

\* Liveness: every entry is eventually resolved -- committed by the rightful
\* leader or discarded once its would-be committer is exposed as stale.
EventualResolution ==
  \A e \in Entries :
    (status[e] \in {"unsubmitted", "pending"}) ~> (status[e] \in {"committed", "discarded"})

====
