CONSTANTS
P1 = P1
P2 = P2
E1 = E1
E2 = E2
InitLeader = P1
MaxTerm = 2
MinCap = 1
MaxCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleCommit
PROPERTY EventualResolution
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
This spec models a bank's interbank settlement batch coordinated by a single elected leader per term, with failover reassigning leadership when needed. Two participants (P1, P2) can be elected leader across up to two terms; each term's authorized leader is recorded permanently in a leader log the moment it is elected. Two pending settlement entries (E1, E2) must first be admitted into a capacity-bounded batch window -- capacity is a runtime-adjustable value, not a fixed constant -- before they can be committed. Only the participant that is both the leader log's recorded authority for the live term AND aware (synced) of that term may commit an entry; a participant still acting on a stale, pre-failover belief has any pending entry it touches discarded rather than committed. This captures the risk that a stale or unauthorized participant, left over after a leadership change, could otherwise sneak an unauthorized settlement commit into the batch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed settlement entry's recorded committer equals the leader that was actually authorized for the term stamped on that commit, so no stale or unauthorized participant's action is ever accepted as a valid commit.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every settlement entry is eventually either committed by the rightful current leader or discarded once its would-be committer is exposed as stale, driven by fairness on admission, authorized commit, stale discard, and belief resynchronization.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m2p0t5 ----
EXTENDS FiniteSets, Naturals

\* Vending machine network: transactions coordinate a two-phase commit
\* to acquire an exclusive vend-slot lock. A privileged admin may also
\* seize the same lock directly, bypassing the vote protocol.
CONSTANTS Txns, Participants

VARIABLES phase, votes, lockHolder, adminHolds

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Txns -> {"idle", "prepared", "committed"}]
  /\ votes \in [Txns -> SUBSET Participants]
  /\ lockHolder \in SUBSET Txns
  /\ adminHolds \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ phase = [t \in Txns |-> "idle"]
  /\ votes = [t \in Txns |-> {}]
  /\ lockHolder = {}
  /\ adminHolds = FALSE

\* Phase 1 of 2PC: coordinator solicits votes from participants.
Prepare(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "idle"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "prepared"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lockHolder, adminHolds>>

Vote(t, p) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "prepared"
  /\ p \notin votes[t]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = @ \union {p}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, lockHolder, adminHolds>>

\* Phase 2 of 2PC: only commits (and takes the lock) once every
\* participant has voted yes, and only if the resource is free.
Commit(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "prepared"
  /\ votes[t] = Participants
  /\ lockHolder = {}
  /\ ~adminHolds
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
  /\ lockHolder' = {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, adminHolds>>

Release(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "committed"
  /\ lockHolder = {t}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ lockHolder' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED adminHolds

\* Admin override: bypasses the vote protocol entirely, but must still
\* respect the mutex by only seizing the slot while it is free.
AdminOverride ==
  /\ ~adminHolds
  /\ lockHolder = {}
  /\ adminHolds' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, lockHolder>>

AdminRelease ==
  /\ adminHolds
  /\ adminHolds' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, lockHolder>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Txns : Prepare(t)
  \/ \E t \in Txns, p \in Participants : Vote(t, p)
  \/ \E t \in Txns : Commit(t)
  \/ \E t \in Txns : Release(t)
  \/ AdminOverride
  \/ AdminRelease

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<phase, votes, lockHolder, adminHolds>>

\* Mutual exclusion of the vend-slot: at most one holder ever, the
\* admin and a committed transaction can never hold it simultaneously,
\* and a committed transaction's identity always matches the holder.
MutualExclusion ==
  /\ Cardinality(lockHolder) <= 1
  /\ (adminHolds => lockHolder = {})
  /\ (lockHolder /= {} => ~adminHolds)
  /\ (\A t \in Txns : phase[t] = "committed" => lockHolder = {t})
  /\ (\A ta, tb \in Txns : (phase[ta] = "committed" /\ phase[tb] = "committed") => ta = tb)

====
nl:
A small network of vending machines shares a single physical vend-slot that
dispenses a scarce item. Any of a small set of transactions may try to
acquire exclusive use of the slot by running a two-phase commit protocol
across the machine's participants: the transaction first asks every
participant to vote (prepare phase), and only once every participant has
voted yes does the transaction commit and take the lock. Separately, a
privileged administrator can seize the vend-slot directly without running
the vote protocol at all, for emergency restocking or maintenance, but this
override must still respect the same exclusivity rule as ordinary
transactions: it can only seize the slot while it is free, and while the
admin holds it no transaction may commit into it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one entity (a committed two-phase-commit transaction, or the admin override) ever holds the vend-slot lock at the same time, and a committed transaction's identity always matches the recorded lock holder.
